Row.Text: The Good Doctor and the Gauls
Dr Rizal inspects a torque, newly made by a local metalworker. The craftsmanship, the way it catches the light – only Gallic hands could have made this.
They are worn all over Gallic lands.

Rising over the oaks, the first quarter moon shines on a group of Gallic druids, gathered for a healing ritual. As the tribe’s elder plucks mistletoe from the heavy branches, a young man watches eagerly, eyes shining. Though some dream of spear and shield, he dreams of druid robes.
Youth is too valuable to spend studying.
A druid’s life is worth the commitment.

The haunting wail of the carnyx looms over the yells and screams of the gaisatai as they rush the Roman forces. Torque and sword reflect the backs of the once-ordered legion, now scattered in fear and cowardice, scrambling over their fallen comrades in a bid to escape.
Pursue them to the last man.

As the villagers prepare the grave chariot, Gallic elders mark out the burial area for a beloved local woman. In the nearby mountain cave, a bard plays his lyre to summon the gods. Haunting notes harmonize with the gentle laps of the cave river like the sounds of spirits come to carry her soul onward.
May the gods below grant us a peaceful life.
For a woman so loved, only peace awaits.

The smell of rain on the wind drifts in through the library’s portico as the young people dutifully recite the druid’s teachings. One student struggles to recall the days of good omen and asks again why they cannot simply write the lesson down. The druid’s sigh is long-suffering.
An allowance can be made for the calendar.

Members of the local Gallic tribe from {1_story_city} gather on the bridge to offer gifts to the gods in exchange for protection. Each person has brought something they cherish - a shield, a bracelet, a tool. The water glistens as the metal objects sink below its surface.
Offer a cauldron made for the gods.
{1_reward} on Nemeton if it is Adjacent to Water.

Shield, spear, sword, carnyx - the freshly polished equipment stacked against the wall catches the eye of the rix's young son. Curious, the boy picks up the carnyx and blows. An eerie wail explodes from the trumpet, startling a sleeping cat who yowls and dashes through the room, scattering the rix’s gear in a cacophony of metal.
Proof that the carnyx is tactically brilliant.
This carnyx is a public nuisance!

Tensions are high between a Gallic woman and her neighbor. The great oak that straddles the border between their homesteads has littered the ground with acorns, attracting a horde of chittering squirrels. Now her neighbor is threatening to cut the tree down, putting their long friendship at risk.
Pair up and hunt the squirrels.
Ask Artio and Diana to calm the wildlife.

As the Gallic men prepare to ambush the capital's garrison, a goose waddles near and eyes the men. One wrong move, and it will honk a warning to the enemy inside. The men freeze, but something catches the creature's attention, and it turns away to investigate.

At the goben, the smith wipes his hands on his apron as he finishes another brooch. Rubbing his back, he takes another rod of silver from the forge. With so many orders, there is no time for rest. Rhythmically beating out the metal, his face softens into a smile. Each ring of the hammer is beautiful and calming.
A brooch makes a lovely gift.
Two brooches make a handsome sale.
Before anything else, a gift for Gobannus.

A loud crack interrupts the battle as the enemy’s siege weapon crumbles to the ground. Cheers erupt on the rampart as the warriors celebrate this success. The enemy’s tricks are no match for the ingenuity of Gallic walls.
They will waste their arrows, then we rush.
We are safe thanks to Gallic brilliance.
Press forward for the common liberty of all Gaul.
Free Promotion on highest Level Commander.

With a haggard breath, the Gallic woman crests the hill where the mountain shrine to Dumiatis sits. For a moment, it is as if she sees what the gods see - an endless blue sky and hills across the landscape dotted with Gallic settlements. Rejuvenated, she leaves her offering and heads back down the trail to home.
On every hill, a Gallic home.

A Gaulish trade fair is always an exercise in chaos. Merchants seeking to hash out a deal try first one dialect of Gaulish, then another, then a third. Some pay in coins of another realm, others still pull forth bags of golden nuggets.
Institute standardization - this is no way to run an empire.

A miniature silver hammer is all that marks the chapter house of the Children of Gobannus, the guild of Gaulish smiths. Inside is a haze of pipe-smoke and whiskey fumes, and the muffled conversation among the leaders of Gaulish industry - gone are the days when Gobannus ruled the blacksmith’s forge; now he is the patron deity of the industrialist.
Surely such exclusivity limits real progress.
